accepted_claims: The literal ordinary-canonical question with nonempty reduced boundary has the plane-quartic counterexample.
The smooth weighted surface has first birational and embedding exponent five.
The smooth monogenic cyclic plane covers have exact threshold ceil(d/((n-1)d-3)), at most four.
Degree five separates all length-two schemes contained scheme-theoretically in the reduced conductor union boundary.
For I>=2, degree five separates every length-two scheme contracted by degree three.
For I>=2, degree five separates every length-two scheme avoiding the base locus of degree two.
For I>=2, basepoint-freeness in degree two implies very ampleness in degree five.
At index one, the numerical criterion on an available reduced log-well-behaved degree-three curve leaves exactly (degree,arithmetic genus)=(1,3),(2,5).
remaining_gap: For I>=2, possible degree-five failures meeting the degree-two base locus but already separated by degree three, and not contained in the conductor union boundary. At index one, curve construction/global generation and the two low-degree numerical cases additionally remain unresolved.
novelty: No novelty claim certified; correct elementary optimization of published machinery.
